chunks: Wiring an SPI bus. The question: How do I make the connections?
Wiring SPI means connecting four signal wires between the master and the slave (clock, two data wires, and chip select), plus ground and power.
The rule is simple: every wire runs from one chip's output pin to the other chip's input pin. The usual mistake is with names.
Slave pins are often labeled SDI and SDO, from the slave's own point of view, so it is easy to cross the data wires.
Think of two people talking. Each has a mouth (an output) and an ear (an input). The wiring rule is mouth to ear, never mouth to mouth.
The master's data-out wire goes to the slave's data-in pin. The slave's data-out wire comes back to the master's data-in pin.

Four signal wires: SCLK and MOSI leave the master through 33 ohms source resistors, MISO returns from the slave's SDO, and CS goes to the slave's CS with a 10 kilohms pull-up so the slave stays deselected while the master's GPIO is floating at reset.
Each chip also needs VDD and a 100 nanofarads capacitor (not drawn).
MOSI and MISO: master-out-slave-in and master-in-slave-out. These names are from the master's point of view.
SDI and SDO: data in and data out, named from the slave's own point of view. Master MOSI goes to slave SDI. Chip select (CS): the wire that picks the slave. It is active when low.
Pull-up resistor: a resistor from a wire to the supply, holding it high when nothing else drives it.
Decoupling capacitor: a small capacitor next to a chip's power pin that supplies quick bursts of current.
Connect master SCLK to slave SCLK. Connect master MOSI to slave SDI. Connect slave SDO to master MISO. Connect a spare master pin to slave CS.
Join the two grounds, and place a 100 nanofarads capacitor at each chip's power pin. Add a 10 kilohms pull-up on CS.
While the microcontroller is still starting up, its pin floats (nothing drives it high or low), and the pull-up keeps the slave from mistaking noise for a command.
Data lines need no pull-ups. That is the whole idea.

"Four wires, function to function: SCLK to SCLK, MOSI from the master's output to the slave's data input, MISO from the slave's data output to the master's input, and CS from a master GPIO to the slave's active-low select.
Common ground and a decoupling cap on each chip.
No pull-ups on the data lines since the drivers are push-pull, but a pull-up on CS keeps the slave deselected at boot, and series resistors help at high clock rates.
More slaves share the three lines and each gets its own CS."
